Two owners belong to the same household when their last names match and their addresses match, 25 * each compared case-insensitively after collapsing runs of whitespace to a single space and 26 * trimming, so trivial differences in spacing or letter case still count as a match. 27 */ 28 final class HouseholdNormalizer { 29 30 private HouseholdNormalizer() { 31 } 32 33 /** 34 * Determines whether two owners, identified by their last name and address, belong to the same 35 * household. Both fields are compared using {@link #normalize(String)}, so the match ignores letter 36 * case and trivial differences in whitespace. 37 * 38 * @param lastNameA the first owner's last name 39 * @param addressA the first owner's address 40 * @param lastNameB the second owner's last name 41 * @param addressB the second owner's address 42 * @return {@code true} if both owners share the same normalized last name and address 43 */ 44 static boolean sameHousehold(String lastNameA, String addressA, String lastNameB, String addressB) { 45 return normalize(lastNameA).equals(normalize(lastNameB)) 46 && normalize(addressA).equals(normalize(addressB)); 47 } 48 49 /** 50 * Normalizes a value for household comparison: leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed, every 51 * internal run of whitespace is collapsed to a single space, and the result is lower-cased so the 52 * comparison is case-insensitive. 53 * 54 * @param value the raw last name or address value, or {@code null} 55 * @return the normalized value, or the empty string when {@code value} is {@code null} 56 */ 57 static String normalize(String value) { 58 if (value == null) { 59 return ""; 60 } 61 return value.trim().replaceAll("\\s+", " ").toLowerCase(); 62 } 63 64 } 65

    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized by
            removing every non-digit character and must contain exactly 10 digits
            after stripping; the normalized 10-digit value is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional; when omitted on create it defaults to the server's current
            date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Request-only flag used on create. When true, the owner may be created
            even though another owner already has the same last name and address
            (i.e. they knowingly share a household). When false or omitted, such a
            request is rejected with 409 Conflict. Not persisted and not returned.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vets (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  first_name VARCHAR(30),
  last_name VARCHAR(30),
  INDEX(last_name)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS specialties (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(80),
  INDEX(name)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vet_specialties (
  vet_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  specialty_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (vet_id) REFERENCES vets(id),
  FOREIGN KEY (specialty_id) REFERENCES specialties(id),
  UNIQUE (vet_id,specialty_id)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS types (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(80),
  INDEX(name)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS owners (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  first_name VARCHAR(30),
  last_name VARCHAR(30),
  address VARCHAR(255),
  city VARCHAR(80),
  telephone VARCHAR(20),
  email VARCHAR(255),
  registration_date DATE,
  customer_code VARCHAR(20),
  INDEX(last_name)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pets (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(30),
  birth_date DATE,
  type_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  owner_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  INDEX(name),
  FOREIGN KEY (owner_id) REFERENCES owners(id),
  FOREIGN KEY (type_id) REFERENCES types(id)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS visits (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  pet_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  visit_date DATE,
  description VARCHAR(255),
  FOREIGN KEY (pet_id) REFERENCES pets(id)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  username VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL ,
  password VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL ,
  enabled TINYINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 ,
  PRIMARY KEY (username)
) engine=InnoDB;

  username varchar(20) NOT NULL,
  role varchar(20) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  UNIQUE KEY uni_username_role (role,username),
  KEY fk_username_idx (username),
  CONSTRAINT fk_username FOREIGN KEY (username) REFERENCES users (username)
) engine=InnoDB;

## Summary

I implemented the `sharesHousehold` / `householdId` feature in the Spring PetClinic REST app. The household **duplicate-rejection** and `sharesHousehold` opt-in logic already existed; the missing piece was assigning and returning a stable shared `householdId`.

Changes:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — Added a read-only `householdId` string to the `Owner` response schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` exposes it.

2. **`model/Owner.java`** — Added the `householdId` field (`@Column(name = "household_id")`) with getter/setter. MapStruct auto-maps it into `OwnerDto`.

3. **`v1/HouseholdNormalizer.java`** — Added `householdId(lastName, address)`, which derives a stable, opaque identifier (first 16 hex chars of SHA-256) purely from the **normalized** last name + address. Because it reuses the same normalization as the existing `sameHousehold` match, any two owners that share a household deterministically derive the *same* id — no cross-owner state coordination needed.

4. **`v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — Assigns `owner.setHouseholdId(...)` on create. Every owner in a given household gets the same value, so joiners created with `sharesHousehold=true` share one identifier, which is returned in the response and via `GET /api/owners/{id}`.

5. **Schema/seed SQL** — Added the `household_id` column to all four `schema.sql` files (hsqldb/h2/mysql/postgres) and appended the matching `NULL` to the positional owner inserts in the hsqldb `data.sql` (the one the tests use).

The new `coreJoinersShareHouseholdId` acceptance test — which creates two owners sharing a first owner's last name + address with `sharesHousehold=true` and asserts they return an identical, non-blank `householdId` — now passes, and so does the full suite.

Note: the `mysql`/`postgres`/`h2` seed data was already out of sync with its own schema before this change (e.g. the mysql owners inserts predate `customer_code`) and isn't exercised by tests, so I left those seeds alone rather than fix pre-existing unrelated drift — happy to bring them into sync if you'd like.
